A.explanation: Too small by a factor of about 10, from an error in combining $m$, $g$, $v$, $I$ and $V$ for the 14 000 kg container.

B.explanation: Too small by a factor of about 10, consistent with omitting the $3.2 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ speed when finding useful power $mgv$.

C.explanation: Much less than the ratio of about $440 \text{ kW}$ useful power to $528 \text{ kW}$ input power for the 240 A, 2200 V motor.

D.explanation: Matches $mgv/IV$ for the lifting container, about $439000/528000 \approx 0.83$ or 83%.

hints: Notice the two powers: electrical power supplied to the 240 A, 2200 V motor and mechanical power gained by the 14 000 kg container moving at $3.2 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Recall efficiency = useful power output / total power input, with input $P = IV$ and output for steady lifting $P = Fv = mgv$.
Calculate $P_{in} = 240 \times 2200$ and $P_{out} = 14000 \times 9.81 \times 3.2$, then divide and multiply by 100% to compare with 8.1%, 8.5%, 48% and 83%.
walkthrough: Identify input power to the motor: $P_{in} = IV$, with $I = 240 \text{ A}$ and $V = 2200 \text{ V}$.
Calculate $P_{in} = 240 \times 2200 = 528000 \text{ W}$, the total electrical power supplied.
Identify useful output power: the container of mass $m = 14000 \text{ kg}$ rises steadily at $v = 3.2 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, so lifting force equals weight $F = mg$.
Use $P_{out} = Fv = mgv = 14000 \times 9.81 \times 3.2 \approx 439000 \text{ W}$ in $\text{W}$ or $\text{J s}^{-1}$.
Apply efficiency = $P_{out}/P_{in} = 439000/528000 \approx 0.832$, giving about 83% after multiplying by 100%.
